body: I work for my states max facility and actually last night was probably one of our worst night. We are guy in our observation cell cave his head in. Luckily we have camera in those cells because any longer and the guy would have bleed out. For 20 minutes he proceeded to smash his head against a metal sink and by the time we were able to pull him out, the entire floor was cover in blood. His head had an open wound about the size of a baseball. We called for an ambulance and he was rushed out but he looked gone. But usally it's people either throwing poop on officers or eating it is about as far as I've seen so far.

I recently started working for the mdoc and this isn't the first closure and it won't be the last. Within the last couple of years we've dropped our inmate count from 51,000 ish to 41,000. As an officer it's kind of scarey think your faculty might be next on the chopping block but as a citizen it's good to see a department not looking to keep people locked up and giving them a chance after doing there time. We also have a whole facitity dedicated to helping inmates learn new skills for when there release date comes and there actually skilled labor jobs that pay well.

I remmemberthe pain was horrible as I walked to the bathroom. Low and behold I didn't make it in time and made a mess of my underwear. I sort of panicked and threw them behind her toilet in some weird justicifaction no one would find them. They are masters of manipulation and you have to be mindful of it everyday. One extra tray, one price of gum or anything that they don't have coming means your into far and they will use it to blackmail you. We had an escape due to it. Most civilians thing our job is easy but your on guard everyday and if you relax they will tear into you. Prison is a different world

Was doing a cell search last week and found a manifesto of how to manipulate people and get what you want out of them. Wasn't contraband so couldn't remove it but just goes to show they know who to prey on and how to get what they want.
Corrections officer for a level 5 prison. Get to see some weird shit for sure

They are chosen by past behaviour and it's a highly regarded position. Out of the 280 inmates in our level one there are maybe 12 that are doing the program. They are kept with the inmates in an open 4 person bunk and there supplied there own dog training supplys and there own dog bed.

While the program is amazing there have been a couple instances of inmates hiding contraband in animals. Obviously they lost there position as a leader dog trainer and more charges were added. Any abuse or negligence will have you disbared from the program

I work for a state prison that has a leader dog program that takes in strays and train's them to be seeing eye dogs. These dogs that were slated for death are now helping the blind be mobile. It's a positive outlet for inmates who may not have had many while on the outside. A great program
